title: Ransomware_Incident_Response_Scenario_1a9
description: Investigate a ransomware incident on a Linux system, identify the threat, and contain the damage.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim host in your network has been compromised by ransomware. Your task is to investigate the incident, identify the threat, and contain the damage. The victim host is running a Linux operating system and has been exhibiting unusual behavior.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation

levels.title: Identify the Command-and-Control Server
levels.content:
Identify the external host communicating with the compromised system.

Question: What is the IP address of the command-and-control server?

Hint: Check network connections and logs for suspicious outbound connections.
levels.solution: To identify the command-and-control server, you need to check network connections and logs for suspicious outbound connections. Use commands like `netstat -tuln` or `ss -tuln` to list active connections. Look for connections to external IPs that are not part of your internal network.

hints.title: Network Connections
hints.content: Use commands like `netstat -tuln` or `ss -tuln` to list active connections.

hints.title: Log Analysis
hints.content: Check logs in `/var/log/` for suspicious outbound connections.

levels.title: Determine the Command-and-Control Port
levels.content:
Determine which network port is used for suspicious command-and-control communication.

Question: What is the port number used for the command-and-control communication?

Hint: Investigate network traffic to identify unusual ports.
levels.solution: To determine the command-and-control port, investigate network traffic to identify unusual ports. Use tools like `tcpdump` or `Wireshark` to capture and analyze network traffic. Look for connections to external IPs on non-standard ports.

hints.title: Network Traffic Analysis
hints.content: Use tools like `tcpdump` or `Wireshark` to capture and analyze network traffic.

hints.title: Port Scanning
hints.content: Use `nmap` to scan for open ports and identify suspicious activity.

levels.title: Identify Exfiltrated Files
levels.content:
Identify a file or a dataset that was transferred outside the environment before encryption.

Question: What is the name of a file that was exfiltrated from the victim host?

Hint: Analyze logs and network activity to determine what data was exfiltrated.
levels.solution: To identify exfiltrated files, analyze logs and network activity to determine what data was exfiltrated. Check logs in `/var/log/` for any references to file transfers or exfiltration. Use tools like `rsync` to verify the presence of exfiltrated files on the exfil-server.

hints.title: Log Analysis
hints.content: Check logs in `/var/log/` for any references to file transfers or exfiltration.

hints.title: Network Activity
hints.content: Use tools like `Wireshark` to capture and analyze network traffic for exfiltration.
